generators.carrier: declared finite matrix P with Z2 parity data

relations.statement: P*P = I for declared finite matrix P; on eigenvalues lambda in {1,-1}, lambda*lambda = 1
relations.hypotheses: P is a declared finite matrix; eigenvalue case needs lambda = 1 or lambda = -1

relations.statement: P*H = H*P for declared finite effective Hamiltonian H
relations.hypotheses: H and P are declared finite matrices of the same dimension; no readout model assumed

lemmas.statement: If lambda = 1 or lambda = -1 then lambda*lambda = 1 (scalar shadow of P^2 = I)
lemmas.lean_skeleton: example (lambda : Int) (h : lambda = 1 ∨ lambda = -1) : lambda * lambda = 1 := parity_eigenvalues lambda h

lemmas.statement: For declared finite matrices P, H: P*P = 1 and P*H = H*P are algebraic checks; C_Q shifts and reflectometry signals are not inputs and imply neither protection nor coherence
lemmas.lean_skeleton: theorem fence {n : Nat} (P H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) Int) (h1 : P * P = 1) (h2 : P * H = H * P) : P * P = 1 ∧ P * H = H * P := ⟨h1, h2⟩

near_misses.claim: gamma_1 restricted to a parity sector commutes with P
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: gamma_1 maps even to odd sector so [gamma_1,P] is nonzero; already refused

near_misses.claim: A measured C_Q shift or reflectometry signal establishes topological protection or coherence
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: No experimental readout model is derived; these are external models, not algebraic properties of the finite matrices
